_documentation: Framework catalog for configs/control-mappings.json. Each framework key lists the source version, publication date, the URLs used to verify identifiers, and the control identifiers Auditex is allowed to map to. Titles are short Auditex paraphrases for orientation only; read the source benchmark for the authoritative wording. A control id that is not listed here must not appear in control-mappings.json for that key (tests/test_framework_baselines.py enforces this). See docs/reference/framework-mappings.md.

cyber_essentials.title: Cyber Essentials: Requirements for IT Infrastructure
cyber_essentials.question_set: Danzell (IASME self-assessment question set for v3.3)
cyber_essentials.id_format: Auditex-local requirement id ce.<theme>.<name>. The NCSC document has no numbered requirements, so each id cites the heading path as printed in the document.
cyber_essentials.document_title: Cyber Essentials: Requirements for IT Infrastructure v3.3
cyber_essentials.effective_note: NCSC lists v3.3 as the current Requirements for IT infrastructure, dated 27 April 2026. IASME applies it to assessment accounts created after 26 April 2026 (its November 2025 notice says 27 April); accounts created earlier keep v3.2 for six months, so both versions are in use until late October 2026.

related_documents.title: Cyber Essentials Plus Test Specification
related_documents.note: No v3.3 test specification exists; NCSC still lists v3.2 as current for CE+ assessments.

requirement_statuses.automated: Tenant evidence alone can decide the whole requirement. No Cyber Essentials requirement qualifies in this version: each one also spans devices, other cloud services or organisational practice.
requirement_statuses.partial: Tenant evidence covers part of the requirement. A rule can show a gap, and the requirement then fails; a clean result is recorded as not assessed, never as pass, because it says nothing about the rest.
requirement_statuses.manual: The applicant answers and evidences it. Auditex has no tenant evidence and reports no verdict.
requirement_statuses.ce_plus_assessor_test: The CE+ assessor tests it technically. Auditex reports no verdict; any rules listed are supporting evidence only.
requirement_statuses.provider_responsibility: The cloud provider typically implements it for SaaS. The applicant must hold the contractual commitment. Auditex reports no verdict.

mapping_confidence.full: The rule tests the condition the requirement names, for the audited tenant.
mapping_confidence.partial: The rule tests a proxy or a subset of the condition, for example registration rather than enforcement.
mapping_confidence.supporting: The rule is listed as supporting evidence only. It shows what Auditex saw, and it never decides the requirement's status: a failing supporting rule does not fail the requirement.

cyber_essentials.disclaimer: Auditex output is evidence for a Cyber Essentials assessor. It is not a Cyber Essentials assessment, certificate or CE+ result, and a pass here never replaces the applicant's own answers or the assessor's tests.

ce.fw.device_firewall.title: Every in-scope device is protected by a correctly configured firewall
ce.fw.device_firewall.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 1. Firewalls > Requirements
ce.fw.device_firewall.evidence_limits: Device and network firewalls are not visible to a tenant audit. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.fw.admin_interface.title: Firewall default administrative passwords changed and the admin interface not exposed to the internet without MFA or an IP allow list
ce.fw.admin_interface.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 1. Firewalls > Requirements
ce.fw.admin_interface.evidence_limits: Boundary device configuration is outside the Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace APIs. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.fw.inbound_rules.title: Unauthenticated inbound connections blocked by default; inbound rules approved, documented and removed when unneeded
ce.fw.inbound_rules.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 1. Firewalls > Requirements
ce.fw.inbound_rules.evidence_limits: Firewall rule sets and their approval records are not collected. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.fw.internet_exposure.title: Only secure and necessary network services can be reached from the internet
ce.fw.internet_exposure.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 1. Firewalls > Aim
ce.fw.internet_exposure.evidence_limits: The CE+ assessor scans every internet-facing address in scope. Auditex DNS posture rules do not test open services.

ce.fw.saas_provider.title: For SaaS, the cloud provider implements the firewall control; the applicant holds the contractual commitment
ce.fw.saas_provider.citation: D. Scope > (iv) Cloud services > Table 1: Explanation of who may typically implement each control
ce.fw.saas_provider.evidence_limits: Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace are SaaS. The applicant must hold the provider's contractual or trust-centre commitment. Auditex cannot see it.

ce.sc.unnecessary_accounts.title: Unnecessary user accounts, such as unused administrative accounts, removed or disabled
ce.sc.unnecessary_accounts.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 2. Secure Configuration > Requirements > Computers and network devices
ce.sc.unnecessary_accounts.evidence_limits: Covers inactive tenant accounts only. Local and device accounts, guest accounts on devices and unused service accounts are not checked.

ce.sc.default_passwords.title: Default or guessable account passwords changed
ce.sc.default_passwords.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 2. Secure Configuration > Requirements > Computers and network devices
ce.sc.default_passwords.evidence_limits: Auditex never tests credentials. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.sc.unnecessary_software.title: Unnecessary software, utilities and network services removed or disabled
ce.sc.unnecessary_software.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 2. Secure Configuration > Requirements > Computers and network devices
ce.sc.unnecessary_software.evidence_limits: Installed software and services on devices are not collected. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.sc.autorun_disabled.title: Auto-run that executes files without user authorisation disabled
ce.sc.autorun_disabled.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 2. Secure Configuration > Requirements > Computers and network devices
ce.sc.autorun_disabled.evidence_limits: Device configuration profiles are not normalised. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.sc.user_authentication.title: Users authenticated before access to organisational data or services
ce.sc.user_authentication.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 2. Secure Configuration > Requirements > Computers and network devices
ce.sc.user_authentication.evidence_limits: Anonymous or unauthenticated access to organisational services is not tested as a requirement. The rules that report anyone links and public sharing are listed as supporting evidence only. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.sc.device_unlocking.title: Device unlocking credentials in place and protected against brute force; PIN or password of at least 6 characters
ce.sc.device_unlocking.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 2. Secure Configuration > Requirements > Device unlocking credentials
ce.sc.device_unlocking.evidence_limits: Intune compliance settings (passcode, minimum passcode length, encryption) are collected into compliance_policy_objects.json but no Auditex rule judges them. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.sc.saas_configuration.title: SaaS cloud services configured securely and providing only the services required
ce.sc.saas_configuration.citation: D. Scope > (iv) Cloud services; E. Requirements by technical control theme > 2. Secure Configuration > Aim
ce.sc.saas_configuration.evidence_limits: Covers legacy authentication (the Conditional Access block and tenant-wide SMTP AUTH) and user app consent only. Other SaaS settings are not tested against this requirement.

ce.sum.supported_software.title: All in-scope software is licensed and supported, and removed when it becomes unsupported
ce.sum.supported_software.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 3. Security Update Management > Requirements
ce.sum.supported_software.evidence_limits: Covers the operating system of devices enrolled in Intune, judged against the dated table in configs/os-end-of-life.json, and ChromeOS devices past their auto-update expiry in Google Workspace. Applications, firmware, Windows Server and devices managed by neither Intune nor Google Workspace are not covered. A Windows build that Long-Term Servicing (LTSC, LTSB or IoT) editions share, or whose Home/Pro date has passed while Enterprise and Education is still supported, is unknown because osVersion does not show the edition; a release the table does not list is unknown too. A clean result is recorded as not assessed, never as a pass.

ce.sum.automatic_updates.title: Automatic updates enabled where possible
ce.sum.automatic_updates.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 3. Security Update Management > Requirements
ce.sum.automatic_updates.evidence_limits: Covers Windows Update for Business update rings read from Intune: whether a ring is assigned and whether it delays quality updates. macOS, iOS, Android and application updates, Windows Update settings made by group policy or other tools, and devices that are not enrolled are not covered, and a ring assigned to a group is not resolved to devices.

ce.sum.vulnerability_fixes_14_days.title: Critical and high-risk updates and vulnerability fixes installed within 14 days of release
ce.sum.vulnerability_fixes_14_days.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 3. Security Update Management > Requirements
ce.sum.vulnerability_fixes_14_days.evidence_limits: Partial evidence only: update rings that delay quality updates beyond 14 days, devices that have not synced within the stale-sync window (14 days by default), and operating systems past end of life or auto-update expiry. Intune noncompliance is listed as supporting evidence only: the compliance state does not say which setting failed, so it never fails this requirement. None of them measures the age of an installed update. The CE+ assessor decides this with an authenticated vulnerability scan of sampled devices.
ce.sum.vulnerability_fixes_14_days.ce_plus_test: Test case 2: Check patching, by authenticated vulnerability scan of devices

ce.sum.saas_provider.title: For SaaS, the cloud provider implements security update management; the applicant holds the contractual commitment
ce.sum.saas_provider.citation: D. Scope > (iv) Cloud services > Table 1: Explanation of who may typically implement each control
ce.sum.saas_provider.evidence_limits: Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace are SaaS. The applicant must hold the provider's commitment. Auditex cannot see it.

ce.uac.account_approval.title: A process to create and approve user accounts
ce.uac.account_approval.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 4. User Access Control > Requirements
ce.uac.account_approval.evidence_limits: Joiner and approval processes are not visible in tenant data. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.uac.unique_credentials.title: Users authenticate with unique credentials before access to applications or devices
ce.uac.unique_credentials.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 4. User Access Control > Requirements
ce.uac.unique_credentials.evidence_limits: Shared accounts cannot be told apart from named accounts in the collected data. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.uac.remove_unused_accounts.title: User accounts removed or disabled when no longer required, including after a defined period of inactivity
ce.uac.remove_unused_accounts.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 4. User Access Control > Requirements
ce.uac.remove_unused_accounts.evidence_limits: Covers inactive enabled tenant accounts only, judged against Auditex's own inactivity threshold (90 days for Microsoft 365 users and administrators, 365 for Google administrators), not the period the applicant has defined. Leavers still active within the window and third-party accounts are not detected.

ce.uac.mfa_cloud_services.title: MFA implemented where available; authentication to cloud services always uses MFA
ce.uac.mfa_cloud_services.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 4. User Access Control > Requirements; E. Requirements by technical control theme > 4. User Access Control > Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
ce.uac.mfa_cloud_services.evidence_limits: Covers the audited Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace tenant only. Every other cloud service the organisation uses needs separate evidence. Per-user (legacy) MFA states are not read, so a Microsoft 365 tenant that enforces MFA only through per-user MFA, without security defaults or Conditional Access, can read fail here. A Conditional Access policy that excludes principals other than the emergency access accounts listed with --break-glass-accounts also fails the requirement. Registration rules show capability, not enforcement.
ce.uac.mfa_cloud_services.ce_plus_test: Test case 4: Check multi-factor authentication configuration

ce.uac.mfa_admin_accounts.title: MFA protects administrative accounts and accounts reachable from the internet
ce.uac.mfa_admin_accounts.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 4. User Access Control > Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
ce.uac.mfa_admin_accounts.evidence_limits: Covers administrator roles in the audited tenant only. Microsoft 365 enforcement is read from security defaults and Conditional Access against the effective administrator set (per-user MFA states are not read); PIM-eligible and group-based administrators depend on the identity collectors completing. Registration rules show capability, not enforcement.
ce.uac.mfa_admin_accounts.ce_plus_test: Test case 4: Check multi-factor authentication configuration

ce.uac.separate_admin_accounts.title: Separate accounts used for administrative activities only
ce.uac.separate_admin_accounts.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 4. User Access Control > Requirements
ce.uac.separate_admin_accounts.evidence_limits: identity.admin_holds_productivity_licence reports administrator accounts that also hold an Exchange Online mailbox or a productivity licence, which is partial evidence only: it does not show whether the administrator uses a different account for daily work. The CE+ assessor tests account separation on sampled devices and cloud environments.

ce.uac.special_access_privileges.title: Special access privileges removed or disabled when no longer required
ce.uac.special_access_privileges.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 4. User Access Control > Requirements
ce.uac.special_access_privileges.evidence_limits: Covers privileged role assignments in the audited tenant: direct, PIM-eligible and inherited through a role-assignable group, as far as the membership fan-out reaches. Only an administrator who has not signed in within the inactivity threshold fails the requirement. The number of administrators, disabled administrators and guest administrators are listed as supporting evidence only: Cyber Essentials sets no count and asks for privileges to be removed or disabled when no longer required. Role changes when staff move are not observed.

ce.uac.password_brute_force.title: Password guessing limited by MFA, throttling or lock-out (no more than 10 guesses in 5 minutes)
ce.uac.password_brute_force.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 4. User Access Control > Password-based authentication
ce.uac.password_brute_force.evidence_limits: Smart lockout and device lock-out settings are not collected. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.uac.password_quality.title: Password quality enforced by MFA, 12 characters, or 8 characters with a deny list
ce.uac.password_quality.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 4. User Access Control > Password-based authentication
ce.uac.password_quality.evidence_limits: Password policy and banned-password settings are not collected. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.uac.password_guidance.title: Users supported to choose unique passwords, with no forced expiry or complexity rules and a process to change compromised passwords
ce.uac.password_guidance.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 4. User Access Control > Password-based authentication
ce.uac.password_guidance.evidence_limits: These are organisational practices. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.uac.third_party_accounts.title: Third-party and supplier accounts, such as managed service provider accounts, controlled like internal accounts
ce.uac.third_party_accounts.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 4. User Access Control > Requirements; D. Scope > (v) Accounts used by third parties and managed infrastructure
ce.uac.third_party_accounts.evidence_limits: Supplier accounts cannot be identified from tenant data alone. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.mp.antimalware.title: Anti-malware software active on in-scope devices, kept up to date, preventing malicious code and malicious websites
ce.mp.antimalware.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 5. Malware protection > Requirements > Anti-malware software (option for in scope devices running Windows or MacOS including servers, desktop computers, laptops)
ce.mp.antimalware.evidence_limits: Covers Defender antivirus state read from Intune for Windows devices (antivirus off, real-time protection off, signatures stale) and the default Exchange Online anti-malware policy. macOS, anti-malware products other than Defender, devices Intune does not manage and protection against malicious websites are not covered; a device protected by a third-party product can read as Defender off. The CE+ assessor tests it with malware test files.

ce.mp.app_allow_listing.title: Alternatively, only approved, code-signed applications can run
ce.mp.app_allow_listing.citation: E. Requirements by technical control theme > 5. Malware protection > Requirements > Application allow listing (option for all in scope devices)
ce.mp.app_allow_listing.evidence_limits: Application control policies are not collected. No Auditex rule reads this. Evidence comes from the applicant's answers and the assessor.

ce.mp.saas_provider.title: For SaaS, the cloud provider implements malware protection; the applicant holds the contractual commitment
ce.mp.saas_provider.citation: D. Scope > (iv) Cloud services > Table 1: Explanation of who may typically implement each control
ce.mp.saas_provider.evidence_limits: Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace are SaaS. The applicant must hold the provider's commitment. Auditex cannot see it.
